name: Example: Finding the Formula for the Sum of a Geometric Series Given an Arbitrary Term and the Common Ratio
problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the $3$rd term is $18$ and the common ratio is $3?$
worked_solution:
We use the formula for the $n$th term of a geometric sequence to determine $a_1\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{r}^{n-1} \\ 18 & ={a}_{1}\cdot {3}^{(3-1)} \\ 18 & =9{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
S_N = \dfrac{a_1 (1-r^N) }{1-r}	.
$$

In this case, $a_1=2$ and $r=3.$ Substituting our values into the formula for $S_N$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{2(1-{3}^{N})}{1-3} \\  & =-\frac{2}{2}(1-{3}^{N}) \\  & ={3}^{N}-1.\end{aligned}
$$
